markPoints: Identify dull black disc.
Quote shortest time to reach 35°C: 1.7 min, for otherwise identical discs.

feedback.short: Identify dull black disc. Quote shortest time to reach 35°C: 1.7 min, for otherwise identical discs.

questions.prompt: Figure 7 shows four identical discs exposed to the same infrared lamp. Times to reach 35°C: dull black 1.7 min, shiny black 2.1 min, dull silver 5.6 min and shiny silver 15.0 min. Explain why shiny silver takes the longest.
questions.subject: physics

markPoints: Shiny silver has low absorptivity (and reflects much incoming IR).
Thus energy transfer into it is slower and temperature rises more slowly.

feedback.short: Shiny silver has low absorptivity (and reflects much incoming IR). Thus energy transfer into it is slower and temperature rises more slowly.

questions.prompt: A student wraps a hot potato in shiny aluminium foil. Explain one way the foil may reduce heat loss by infrared radiation, and state a limitation.

This reduces one route of cooling but does not eliminate conduction or convection.

feedback.short: Shiny foil outer surface has low infrared emissivity. It emits less infrared to cooler surroundings than a dull surface. This reduces one route of cooling but does not eliminate conduction or convection.

Particle conduction across vacuum is prevented (glass/stopper still allow some conduction).

questions.prompt: A vacuum flask can keep both hot and cold liquids at a more constant temperature. Explain why.

accepted: Flask slows energy transfer both ways.

questions.prompt: Two otherwise identical kettles, one dull black and one shiny silver, contain the same volume of hot water and are hotter than the room. Explain why the black kettle can cool faster.

accepted: Black finish radiates faster when hotter.

Black/dull surface has higher infrared emissivity than shiny silver.

feedback.short: Both kettles otherwise identical and hotter than surroundings. Black/dull surface has higher infrared emissivity than shiny silver. It transfers more energy away by radiation per second, so may cool faster under equal conditions.

questions.prompt: Explain how the surface finish affects infrared emission, comparing a dull black surface with shiny silver at the same temperature.

accepted: Dull black tends to emit infrared most strongly.

For equal temperature/area, dull black has high emissivity.
Shiny metallic surfaces typically have lower emissivity; visible colour alone does not always determine IR emissivity.

feedback.short: All objects emit IR when above absolute zero. For equal temperature/area, dull black has high emissivity. Shiny metallic surfaces typically have lower emissivity; visible colour alone does not always determine IR emissivity.

questions.prompt: Explain why radiation is the only method of heat transfer that can occur in a vacuum.

feedback.short: Conduction and convection rely on particles. Electromagnetic waves can transfer energy without a medium.

feedback.short: Both cans receive same incoming sunlight and start at same temperature. Dull black absorbs a larger fraction of incoming radiation. Under stated assumption of negligible emission differences over test, black can reach higher temperature.

questions.prompt: A house has a large cold window. Explain how curtain thickness, trapped air, reflective lining and fit can affect heat loss on a cold night. Assess whether visible curtain colour alone is enough to predict infrared heat loss.
questions.subject: physics

markPoints: A thick insulating layer slows heat conduction.
Trapped still air in fabric reduces convection within fabric.
Close-fitting curtains reduce air movement/draughts by window.
Reflective low-emissivity lining facing room can reduce radiative transfer to a cold window.
Visible colour (black versus white) alone does not reliably predict IR emissivity.
Explain overall heat loss depends on material, thickness, lining and installation, not colour alone.

feedback.short: A thick insulating layer slows heat conduction. Trapped still air in fabric reduces convection within fabric. Close-fitting curtains reduce air movement/draughts by window. Reflective low-emissivity lining facing room can reduce radiative transfer to a cold window. Visible colour (black versus white) alone does not reliably predict IR emissivity. Explain overall heat loss depends on material, thickness, lining and installation, not colour alone.

questions.prompt: Compare the advantages and disadvantages of using dull black surfaces and shiny silver surfaces in different situations.

accepted: Black and shiny surfaces suit different jobs.

feedback.short: Dull black efficiently absorbs incoming radiation. Dull black also emits infrared efficiently. Example: solar absorber or radiator (with suitable conditions). Compare limitations: absorbers also emit well, reflectors may impede desired absorption.

questions.prompt: Explain how the Earth’s average temperature can remain approximately constant when absorbed incoming solar radiation balances outgoing radiation. Include reflection and infrared emission.

accepted: Earth's temperature depends on radiation balance.
markPoints: Sun supplies incoming electromagnetic (largely short-wave) radiation.
Some incoming radiation is reflected to space by clouds/surface.
Earth absorbs remaining energy and emits infrared.
Approximate stability requires average incoming absorbed energy to match outgoing energy; greenhouse effect alters this balance.

feedback.short: Sun supplies incoming electromagnetic (largely short-wave) radiation. Some incoming radiation is reflected to space by clouds/surface. Earth absorbs remaining energy and emits infrared. Approximate stability requires average incoming absorbed energy to match outgoing energy; greenhouse effect alters this balance.

feedback.short: Black describes visible-light appearance, not every wavelength. Dull black commonly absorbs IR strongly. Shiny black may absorb IR less than dull black because surface finish matters.
